brief_summary: Three-row comparison ladder showing the outcome of pressing the identical three-key rectangle under three hardware/firmware regimes: no diodes (blocking/2KRO — a key drops or a ghost appears), full diode matrix on the standard USB boot protocol (6KRO ceiling — no ghost, but a 7th simultaneous key still fails to register), and full diode matrix plus NKRO-aware firmware (all keys register, no ceiling). The two diode-protected rows are coral-highlighted; the no-diode row carries a dashed caution outline.
data_sources: key-matrix-ghosting-deep-dive.mdx § 'A diode blocks the backflow — and creates its own tradeoff' — 'A diode matrix alone doesn't guarantee a keyboard can report an unlimited number of simultaneous keys ... The standard USB HID boot protocol can describe at most six non-modifier keys pressed at once ... a condition usually labeled 6KRO.'
https://deskthority.net/wiki/Rollover,_blocking_and_ghosting — defines 'blocking' as the firmware ignoring keys that could cause ghosting, and NKRO as suffering from neither blocking nor ghosting.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_rollover — defines jamming/blocking and n-key rollover detecting input from every key regardless of how many others are pressed.
